whatYouGet: One Carver LGW02 Black wedge in the loft you picked
clubParas: This is the LGW02 with the volume turned down. Same forged body, same grind, same behaviour out of the same lies — the only thing that changed is what it looks like at address.

Blacked-out finish with gold on the clover and the loft stamp, and nothing else. At address it disappears against the grass, which some golfers find easier to aim and others find they miss the gold entirely.
It is the full six-loft lineup, unlike the gold V2, which stops at three.
Right hand only at the moment. That is a real limitation and it is the reason this is not simply the better version of the gold.

videoBrief: 16:9 product film, 40–60s. The pitch is the finish, so shoot it at address in changing light — the club should read almost invisible against grass and then catch the gold on the stamp as it moves.
specSub: Construction is the LGW02's, from the reference guide. The lie figures in the guide are for the three-loft gold lineup, so they are not carried across to six lofts here.

specTabs.aside: Right hand only. The guide documents the LGW02 as a three-loft club; this black finish runs all six, which is a difference worth confirming before the spec table is treated as final.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. Black head at address on grass in flat light, gold clover the only thing that catches. The point of the shot is how little the club announces itself.
look.headline: The one nobody notices until you use it
paras: Gold clubs get comments. That is fine until it is not, and there is a kind of golfer who would rather the club said nothing at all.
This is that club. It still has gold on it — on the clover, on the number — but you have to be standing over it to find any.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same club with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

closeBody: The Black is $109 in every loft, right hand. Sixty days to send it back if it isn't the one.

helpLoft.headline: Start with the wedge you already carry
helpLoft.sub: Wedges work in gaps. Four to six degrees between clubs keeps your distances even and stops two wedges going the same yardage. The Black comes in all six lofts, so a full ladder is available in this finish.
